title: Candidate-conditioned behavioral-history attention ranker
summary: Use a Deep Interest Network-style local activation module to pool a causally truncated user history differently for every candidate video, then fuse the candidate-aware interest vector with ID, metadata, and aggregate inputs in a final scorer.
use_when: Users have heterogeneous histories in which only a subset of prior videos is relevant to a candidate.
The same user receives diverse video candidates, making a single fixed user-history vector too coarse.
Causal recent-video IDs and associated attributes are available at impression time.
avoid_when: Most users have extremely short or empty usable histories.
Per-candidate attention creates unacceptable inference cost relative to the small expected gain.
History items lack informative IDs or attributes after leakage-safe truncation.

title: Causal self-attentive sequence encoder ranker
summary: Encode each user's strictly pre-impression video sequence with a lightweight causal self-attention encoder, combine its last-state representation with the candidate video and context embeddings, and score the displayed impression with a shallow head.
use_when: Timestamp ordering is reliable and sequential transitions or evolving interests are likely to add signal beyond aggregates.
Users have enough prior interactions for sequence modeling after causal truncation.
You can cap history length and use a small transformer to keep training and inference practical.
avoid_when: The target is driven mainly by stable user-video affinity and histories are mostly sparse.
Event timestamps are tied or unreliable enough that causal ordering cannot be implemented safely.
Scarce experiment budget cannot support checking sequence length, dropout, and attention-width sensitivity.

title: Deep & Cross ranker for bounded-order feature interactions
summary: Augment an embedding-plus-MLP scorer with a small Deep & Cross Network branch so that user, video, context, popularity, and history fields receive explicit bounded-degree crosses alongside nonlinear deep interactions.
use_when: Interactions such as user-by-category affinity, video-by-context, and recency-by-history-length are expected to matter.
You want controlled explicit crosses without enumerating manual feature conjunctions.
The embedding-plus-MLP baseline has useful signal but leaves room for better GAUC or nDCG@5.
avoid_when: Most useful information is in the ordered item sequence rather than tabular field interactions.
Feature dimensions or categorical vocabularies are so sparse that extra cross capacity overfits despite regularization.

title: Embedding-plus-MLP pointwise ranker
summary: A compact pointwise scorer that concatenates user/video ID embeddings, metadata embeddings, causal history features, and numeric aggregates before a residual MLP outputs one long-view logit per impression.
use_when: A strong, low-risk architecture baseline is needed before adding specialized interaction or sequence modules.
Candidate lists are short and scoring every displayed impression independently is computationally inexpensive.
You need an architecture that cleanly accommodates all causally available dense and categorical features.
avoid_when: The validation result shows that a candidate-specific reading of behavioral history is consistently valuable.
A simple model already saturates both GAUC and nDCG@5 and scarce experiments are better spent on objective or feature changes.

title: Impression-log fields and availability classes
summary: Classifies all 19 log columns by impression-time availability and records measured auxiliary-label prevalence.
use_when: engineering log features
designing causal histories
choosing auxiliary targets
avoid_when: using current-row outcomes as features

title: Supplied KuaiRand-Pure files and official splits
summary: Records the supplied files, measured row/entity counts, observed dates, and canonical train/validation/test boundaries.
use_when: loading data
checking split boundaries
validating row counts
avoid_when: inferring splits from filenames alone

title: Validation population, label support, and pair novelty
summary: Quantifies validation entity warmth, 98.37% user-video pair novelty, short candidate lists, and zero/mixed/all-positive user groups.
use_when: selecting transferable models
interpreting GAUC versus nDCG
diagnosing segments
avoid_when: calling validation predominantly entity-cold

title: Random-exposure log as a separate distribution
summary: Describes the random-exposure file, its measured prevalence shift, and why it remains separate from official scoring and model selection.
use_when: researching exposure bias
checking robustness across regimes
avoid_when: pooling it into official training or validation without a new protocol

title: User metadata table
summary: Documents user metadata fields, exact missingness, entity coverage, and the need for item/context interactions in within-user ranking.
use_when: building cold-user fallback
crossing user and item features
analyzing user segments
avoid_when: adding only a user-constant score term

title: Video metadata and aggregate-statistics tables
summary: Documents basic video fields, missingness, coverage, and the causal-provenance requirement for aggregate statistics.
use_when: generalizing across unseen pairs
engineering item metadata
auditing aggregate features
avoid_when: using undated snapshot statistics

title: Candidate-group shared representation scoring
summary: Compute candidate-invariant inputs once per displayed candidate group: user embedding, causal history encoder output, user metadata transforms, and group-level numeric features. Broadcast that state across candidate videos and score the complete group in one vectorized call, preserving scores exactly while reducing repeated work.
use_when: Using causal history attention or a sequence encoder for multiple videos shown to the same user at one impression.
Candidate groups are evaluated intact and contain repeated user-side inputs.
CPU or GPU prediction time is a practical constraint.
avoid_when: Each row genuinely has distinct user-side context or a distinct causal cutoff that prevents safe sharing.
The implementation cannot prove that grouped vectorization preserves canonical row order and identical numerical outputs.

title: Dot-product ranker with a small linear residual head
summary: Use a compact user–video dot product as the main affinity score, then add a small linear or one-hidden-layer residual head for causal numeric, metadata, and context features. This provides a materially cheaper comparator to MLP and attention rankers while preserving personalized score variation.
use_when: A fast, low-variance baseline is needed before spending scarce experiments on deeper rankers.
The deployment path may later require efficient batched scoring or approximate inner-product retrieval.
User and video ID embeddings carry substantial predictive signal.
avoid_when: Candidate-specific history attention or complex feature crosses have already shown a clear validated gain worth their added cost.
The target depends primarily on nonlinear context interactions that a shallow residual cannot recover.
required_features: impression-time context and numeric features; optional

title: Frequency-adaptive user and video embedding dimensions
summary: Allocate larger embedding dimensions to frequent user and video IDs and smaller dimensions to rare IDs, projecting every bucket into one common scorer width. Fit frequency buckets only on training data and compare matched parameter budgets against a fixed-width embedding table.
use_when: Embedding tables account for a substantial share of parameters or optimizer-state memory.
Entity frequency is highly long-tailed and rare IDs are prone to overfitting.
A compact model is desired without collapsing all IDs into one small embedding width.
avoid_when: The supplied entity tables are already small enough that memory and training speed are not limiting.
Frequency buckets would be too sparse to estimate reliably or introduce excessive configuration search.

title: Quantized embedding tables with a full-precision hot-row cache
summary: Keep infrequent embedding rows in low precision and retain a bounded full-precision cache for the most frequently accessed training entities. Use per-row scale metadata, a deterministic cache rule based only on training frequencies, and verify score drift before accepting the memory reduction.
use_when: Embedding-table and optimizer-state memory limits batch size, model width, or feasible architecture choices.
Frequent entities dominate accesses and a compact deployment artifact is required.
The runtime supports tested low-precision embedding lookup on the intended Windows/Linux target.
avoid_when: The dataset is small enough that quantization adds engineering risk without a meaningful resource benefit.
Low-precision kernels are unavailable or prediction parity cannot be verified on the target hardware.
Rare-entity ranking quality is a primary concern and dequantization error is concentrated in those rows.

title: Predeclared successive-halving experiment promotion
summary: Screen predeclared configurations using a deterministic low-cost rung, promote only the best few by a fixed composite ranking rule, and rerun promoted candidates at full training fidelity and full frozen validation scoring. Log every rung, seed, budget, and promotion decision to conserve counted experiments without silently changing selection criteria.
use_when: Official experiments are scarce and several credible architecture, objective, or regularization variants compete.
Early epochs or a fixed validation subset have empirically useful rank correlation with full-fidelity results.
The configuration grid and promotion thresholds can be fixed before running trials.
avoid_when: Short-budget rankings are known to be unstable, especially for sequence models or delayed auxiliary-task gains.
The low-fidelity rung changes candidate-group composition, leakage handling, or the official evaluation definition.
The protocol prohibits adaptive allocation of experiment budget across candidates.

title: Frozen displayed-candidate evaluation audit
summary: Evaluate every model on the exact supplied displayed candidate groups and their canonical row order. Audit group completeness, duplicate rows, score coverage, label composition, and denominator handling before metric computation; never replace displayed candidates with sampled negatives for the official result.
use_when: Implementing official within-user GAUC or nDCG@5 scoring
Validating a newly generated prediction artifact
Comparing models whose dataloaders or ranking heads may reorder, drop, or duplicate impressions
avoid_when: Creating an auxiliary retrieval benchmark explicitly defined over a different full-catalog candidate universe
Treating sampled-negative metrics as interchangeable with the fixed official ranking metric

title: Probability calibration and ranking-error audit
summary: Supplement rank metrics with train-fitted calibration diagnostics such as Brier score, log loss, reliability bins, and predicted-positive-rate checks. Inspect errors separately for mixed candidate groups, because a model can preserve ranking while producing unstable probabilities that impair multitask weighting, threshold analyses, and ensemble averaging.
use_when: Training with BCE or multitask binary heads
Averaging predictions or combining score heads
Investigating whether a ranking improvement came with implausibly extreme or collapsed probabilities
avoid_when: Using calibration metrics as a replacement for GAUC or nDCG@5 model selection
Fitting a calibrator on validation labels and then reporting that same validation result
Applying monotonic calibration solely to manufacture a ranking gain

title: Random-exposure generalization audit
summary: Keep official validation ranking as the model-selection target, then score a separately frozen random-exposure holdout as a secondary audit. Compare each model's ordinary-log and random-exposure ranking behavior, with matched support summaries, to detect gains likely tied to the historical exposure policy rather than user preference.
use_when: Assessing whether a model overfits recommendation-policy exposure patterns
Comparing popularity-heavy, causal-history, or debiased variants
Making a final robustness claim after official validation selection is complete
avoid_when: Replacing the fixed official validation score with this audit without an approved protocol change
Mixing random and ordinary impressions into one unstratified metric
Claiming causal policy value when the available random log lacks the required policy and support information

title: Temporal and population-slice ranking dashboard
summary: Decompose validation GAUC and nDCG@5 into predeclared slices: validation time block, user-history depth, user and video frequency bucket, candidate-group size, and zero-positive, mixed, or all-positive label composition. Report support and uncertainty beside each slice rather than selecting models from a single noisy subgroup.
use_when: Checking whether an overall gain is robust across late validation time blocks
Diagnosing cold or sparse-entity failures
Selecting between models with similar aggregate metrics but different deployment risks
avoid_when: Searching many unplanned slices until a favorable result appears
Ranking models by tiny slices with inadequate mixed-label groups
Using slices built from post-impression information unavailable at scoring time

title: Within-user ranking and diagnostic metrics
summary: Explains official and advisory metrics, their weighting, tradeoffs, and interpretation hazards.
use_when: diagnosing every scored experiment
predicting metric-specific effects
avoid_when: never replace fixed evaluation

title: Anchored fractional-factorial ablation plan
summary: Anchor all experiments to one reproducible reference ranker, then test a compact orthogonal set of high-value interventions such as causal history, aggregate features, ranking loss, and auxiliary supervision. Use a fractional-factorial or staged add-remove design to estimate main effects first, reserve only a small number of runs for interactions suggested by shared mechanisms, and retain the same seed, budget, feature availability policy, and checkpoint rule within each comparison block.
use_when: Several proposed improvements overlap and naive sequential additions would obscure attribution.
The project needs to identify which components merit combination.
Feature and objective changes can be toggled independently from a common backbone.
avoid_when: Components are tightly coupled and invalid or meaningless in isolation.
The reference implementation is not yet deterministic enough for controlled comparisons.
The budget cannot support even a minimal baseline-plus-ablation block.
required_features: fixed training seed or seed block

title: Diversity-gated rank ensemble decision
summary: Construct a small final ensemble only from independently useful finalists whose validation score residuals are not nearly identical. Convert each model's scores to within-candidate-group ranks or standardized groupwise scores before averaging, use fixed equal weights or one predeclared coarse weight grid, and require the ensemble to improve the parent models under paired group bootstrap. Prefer diversity across inductive biases, such as dot-product, cross-feature, and sequence-history scorers, rather than ensembling minor hyperparameter variants of one model.
use_when: Several validated models have complementary GAUC and nDCG@5 error patterns.
Prediction artifacts are available in the exact canonical validation order.
A final inference-time increase is acceptable and component models can be reproduced.
avoid_when: Candidate models are highly correlated checkpoint or seed variants with no complementary errors.
The ensemble weights would require extensive adaptive tuning on the frozen validation set.
One component has invalid, missing, nonfinite, or differently ordered predictions.

title: Paired group-bootstrap and multi-seed promotion test
summary: Treat promotion as a paired comparison between a challenger and its parent using their predictions on the identical frozen validation rows. Resample complete displayed candidate groups, recompute the composite plus GAUC and nDCG@5 deltas, and report confidence intervals and win probability. For changes likely to be seed-sensitive, require confirmation across a small fixed set of seeds and promote only if the mean gain clears a predeclared practical margin without a material component-metric regression.
use_when: Observed improvements are small relative to expected training and candidate-group variance.
A new objective, sequence model, or regularizer may have unstable optimization.
Two models produce predictions on exactly the same validation candidate groups.
avoid_when: Only one prediction artifact is available for either model.
Candidate groups cannot be reconstructed reliably from validation rows.
The comparison changes data, labels, or validation membership rather than only the model configuration.
required_features: seed identifiers and deterministic bootstrap seed

title: Predeclared hypothesis ladder with stop and rollback rules
summary: Organize experiments as a short ordered ladder of falsifiable changes from a fixed reference model. Before training, record the expected metric direction, one primary mechanism, required resources, acceptance margin, and rollback rule for each change. Advance only when the preceding change clears its predeclared confirmation criterion; otherwise retain the parent configuration and redirect the next experiment toward a genuinely different failure mode.
use_when: Official experiment IDs are scarce and each submitted run must have a clear purpose.
Several plausible architecture, feature, objective, or training changes compete for a limited budget.
The team needs an auditable reason for why a configuration was promoted or abandoned.
avoid_when: Running a broad exploratory sweep with plentiful inexpensive local compute.
The candidate changes are inseparable because they must be introduced jointly for the method to function.
required_features: experiment ledger with parent run ID

title: Train-prefix proxy screening before frozen-validation confirmation
summary: Screen inexpensive candidate changes on a deterministic proxy derived only from the training period, such as a train-prefix versus late-train temporal split with identical displayed-group evaluation. Use the official frozen validation set only to confirm a small number of proxy winners under full training fidelity. Calibrate the proxy once against a few known baselines, log proxy-to-validation agreement, and do not repeatedly revise the proxy after seeing official-validation outcomes.
use_when: Repeated access to the official validation metric risks adaptive overfitting.
Training data has enough temporal span to construct an earlier-train and later-train proxy split.
Many low-confidence ideas need elimination before consuming official experiments.
avoid_when: The training period is too short or sparse for a representative temporal proxy.
A proposed method relies on information unavailable in the proxy construction.
The official protocol explicitly prohibits any additional derived validation split.

title: Causally truncated behavioral-history features
summary: Represent each impression with features computed only from that user's earlier events: recent-video IDs, recency, history length, and historical category or tag distributions where available.
use_when: Logs can be ordered reliably within user by timestamp or event order.
Earlier interactions are available at inference for each scored impression.
A cheap recency-aware alternative to a full sequential architecture is valuable.
avoid_when: Event ordering is ambiguous or same-time events cannot be safely ordered.
The implementation would use current or future labels, events, or full-validation histories.
required_features: event timestamp or stable event order
historical item attributes; use none when unavailable

title: User and video identity embeddings with cold/OOV handling
summary: Use compact learned embeddings for user and video IDs as the primary personalization signal, with explicit unknown-index handling and frequency-aware regularization for rare entities.
use_when: The validation set contains mostly warm users or videos seen during training.
A simple personalized baseline is needed before adding side features or histories.
Candidate lists require within-user score variation.
avoid_when: IDs are unavailable at scoring time.
Most validation entities are unseen and no side information is available for fallback.

title: Train-prefix smoothed popularity and affinity statistics
summary: Add smoothed, causally available counts and rates for videos, creators or categories, plus user-by-attribute affinities, fitted on training prefixes and backed off for sparse groups.
use_when: IDs and metadata are sparse enough that aggregate evidence can complement embeddings.
The pipeline can enforce train-only fitting and timestamp-prefix lookup.
Rare-item estimates can be shrunk toward global or attribute-level priors.
avoid_when: Aggregate tables include the target row, future events, or validation/test outcomes.
Counts are treated as static when they are unavailable at the actual impression time.
The supplied aggregate-statistics table has unclear causal provenance.
required_features: video attributes or creator fields; use none when unavailable

title: BCE plus LambdaRank-style nDCG@5 hybrid
summary: Combine user-normalized binary cross-entropy with a within-user pairwise logistic term weighted by the absolute nDCG@5 change induced by swapping each positive-negative pair. Start with BCE-dominant weighting and tune one fixed ranking-loss coefficient, targeting top-five order without discarding broad GAUC supervision.
use_when: nDCG@5 trails GAUC or top-ranked errors are the principal failure mode.
Candidate groups have at least some positive-negative pairs and usually exceed one candidate.
A compact metric-aligned change can be tested on top of an established BCE model.
avoid_when: Candidate groups are predominantly size one or have no mixed labels.
The implementation cannot compute group-local ranks and swap deltas without leakage across groups.
Experiment budget cannot support a controlled coefficient comparison against the BCE parent.
required_features: candidate position only for training-group reconstruction

title: Mixed-group ListNet top-one loss
summary: For each mixed-label within-user candidate group, minimize cross-entropy between a label-derived top-one distribution and the softmax of model scores. Exclude zero-positive and all-positive groups from this term, then optionally retain a small BCE anchor so listwise normalization does not erase useful absolute-label supervision.
use_when: Displayed candidate groups are short and can be packed intact into batches.
The experiment seeks a genuinely listwise alternative to pairwise objectives.
Top-of-list competition among several simultaneously scored candidates is important.
avoid_when: Most groups have only one item or homogeneous labels.
Group reconstruction is ambiguous or batch memory prevents complete groups.
A label-derived probability distribution would be dominated by unreliable graded or duplicated targets.

title: Shared-trunk auxiliary-behavior multitask loss
summary: Attach lightweight binary heads for measured auxiliary engagement labels to the same ranker trunk, retain a dedicated long-view head for scoring, and optimize a weighted sum of user-normalized BCE losses. Keep long-view dominant; admit an auxiliary task only when its label is impression-time valid, sufficiently prevalent, and positively useful on validation.
use_when: The supplied log has auxiliary outcome labels with adequate support.
Long-view positives are sparse and the base model appears variance-limited.
Shared user, video, context, and history representations are already available.
avoid_when: An auxiliary label leaks post-impression information into input features or is unavailable on validation.
Auxiliary-task weighting harms the primary GAUC or nDCG@5 in a fixed ablation.
The auxiliary behavior represents a conflicting preference rather than an earlier or related engagement signal.
required_features: one or more auxiliary outcome labels

title: User-normalized pointwise binary cross-entropy
summary: Train the long-view logit with numerically stable binary cross-entropy, weighting each impression inversely by its user candidate-count so prolific users do not dominate a GAUC-style within-user objective. Use this as the low-variance reference objective and preserve raw probabilities for diagnostics.
use_when: A reliable first neural-ranker objective is needed under scarce experiment budget.
The scorer needs a stable supervised signal on every labeled impression.
Candidate lists contain many zero/mixed/all-positive groups, making pure ranking losses partially undefined or uninformative.
avoid_when: The sole objective must explicitly prioritize top-five swaps and a stable pointwise baseline has already plateaued.
Labels are missing or are not available for every scored training impression.

title: Within-user RankNet pairwise ranking loss
summary: Construct preference pairs only within the same displayed user candidate group, with a positive long-view impression preferred to a negative one, and optimize logistic score differences. Sample a bounded number of negatives per positive to control cost while directly training the ordering used by GAUC.
use_when: Validation GAUC is the limiting metric and mixed-label user groups are sufficiently common.
The model can batch impressions by user candidate group.
A ranking-focused alternative to pointwise BCE is required without listwise softmax instability.
avoid_when: Most training groups are homogeneous, because they yield no valid positive-negative pairs.
Cross-user negatives would be needed to create pairs; these are misaligned with within-user scoring.
Pair enumeration is too large and negative sampling cannot be made deterministic.

title: Predeclared group-DRO within-user ranking objective
summary: Optimize a robust mixture of group-complete ranking losses by upweighting predeclared high-loss groups, such as late training periods, sparse-history users, rare videos, or candidate-group-size buckets. Combine the group-DRO term with strong regularization and early stopping, because worst-group optimization alone can overfit neural models; retain the ordinary objective as an anchor to protect the primary aggregate metric. ([mlanthology.org](https://mlanthology.org/iclr/2020/sagawa2020iclr-distributionally/?utm_source=openai))
use_when: Temporal and population-slice evaluation reveals repeatable regressions despite acceptable aggregate GAUC and nDCG@5.
A model is suspected of exploiting correlations concentrated in frequent entities or historical periods.
Predeclared groups have enough complete mixed-label candidate groups to estimate stable losses.
avoid_when: Slice deficits are based on tiny supports or are not stable under paired group bootstrap.
The optimization budget cannot support tracking per-group moving losses and weights.
The intended groups encode protected attributes without an approved fairness and governance protocol.
required_features: predeclared training-only temporal, frequency, history-depth, or group-size assignments
ordinary user-normalized BCE or within-group ranking anchor

title: Multi-gate mixture-of-experts auxiliary-behavior ranker
summary: Replace a fully shared multitask trunk with a small multi-gate mixture-of-experts model: share 2–4 compact experts, learn a task-specific gate for long-view and each admitted auxiliary behavior, and retain a long-view-dominant user-normalized BCE or ranking loss. MMoE explicitly adapts sharing to task relatedness, addressing negative transfer from weak auxiliary labels. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1145/3219819.3220007?utm_source=openai))
use_when: At least one impression-time-valid auxiliary engagement label has adequate prevalence and a shared-trunk multitask baseline is neutral or inconsistent.
Different behaviors plausibly depend on different mixtures of user, item, context, and history signals.
A compact change is preferred over independently training several task-specific rankers.
avoid_when: Only the long-view label is reliable or auxiliary labels are too sparse.
Auxiliary labels contain post-impression information forbidden by the availability policy.
Compute limits cannot support even a small multi-head model; use the existing shared trunk instead.
required_features: one or more impression-time-valid auxiliary binary labels

title: Clipped IPS-weighted within-group ranking loss
summary: Replace the ordinary contribution of each observed long-view label with a stabilized clipped inverse-exposure-propensity weight, then optimize weighted BCE or weighted positive-negative RankNet pairs only within complete displayed candidate groups. Normalize weights within minibatches and cap both individual and group total weight so rare-propensity examples improve exposure robustness without dominating the ranking signal.
use_when: The propensity-overlap gate passes and exposure probabilities describe the data-generating display mechanism.
A strong unweighted BCE or RankNet baseline is already available for a one-variable comparison.
The expected bias concerns are primarily position, presentation, or selective-exposure bias rather than label-definition error.
avoid_when: Propensities are unavailable, estimated from post-impression variables, or have severe non-overlap.
The random-exposure sample is too small to substantiate an exposure-bias motivation.
Training becomes unstable after predeclared clipping and normalization; retain the unweighted baseline rather than repeatedly tuning clipping thresholds.
required_features: pre-impression covariates used to estimate propensity when propensities are not logged

title: Doubly robust exposure-debiased ranking objective
summary: Combine a direct long-view outcome model with a propensity-corrected residual loss: train the ranking model on an imputed outcome term plus a clipped IPS correction for observed-label errors. Cross-fit or isolate nuisance-model fitting from scored folds, keep the final scorer group-aware, and compare against both ordinary and IPS-only objectives to determine whether the imputation model reduces high-variance propensity correction.
use_when: Propensities pass overlap checks but IPS-only training is noisy or sensitive to reasonable clipping levels.
There is adequate training support to fit both an outcome/imputation model and a propensity model using only pre-impression information.
The experiment budget supports a clearly predeclared three-way test: ordinary baseline, IPS, and doubly robust.
avoid_when: Neither propensity nor outcome nuisance models can be validated independently.
The random-exposure data has negligible coverage of important users, videos, or contexts, making nuisance-model extrapolation dominant.
Implementation cannot enforce fold separation or train-only fitting for imputation and propensity models.
required_features: exposure propensity or train-fitted propensity estimate
imputation-model inputs restricted to impression-time availability
fold or temporal split identifier for nuisance-model isolation

title: Recency-weighted causal ranking training
summary: Apply a bounded exponential time-decay multiplier to complete training candidate groups, preserving within-group labels and user normalization while giving recent impressions more influence. Select only from a short predeclared half-life grid, normalize total training weight, and retain a nonzero minimum weight for older groups so the ranker adapts to preference or inventory drift without catastrophically forgetting sparse entities.
use_when: Chronological validation or the temporal slice dashboard indicates recent-period ranking degradation.
Timestamps are reliable and all recency weights are computed relative to the training cutoff, never future validation data.
The catalog, popularity distribution, or engagement behavior plausibly changes over the observation window.
avoid_when: The official split is effectively i.i.d. or temporal analysis shows no material drift.
The recent period is too small or label-sparse to support stronger weighting.
Timestamps, event ordering, or cutoff handling are ambiguous and could introduce future information.

title: Counted-experiment and convergence protocol
summary: Defines what consumes an experiment ID, how parent 0 differs from evidence, and why hypotheses must be selective under the stopping rule.
use_when: prioritizing hypotheses
checking experiment references
interpreting convergence
avoid_when: treating screening or abandoned attempts as scored evidence

title: KuaiRand within-user long-view ranking
summary: Defines the fixed target, official ranking metrics, within-user scope, and consequences for useful score variation.
use_when: checking task compatibility
interpreting candidate gains
avoid_when: never exclude from fixed context

title: Impression-time availability and leakage policy
summary: Defines impression-time feature availability, current-outcome exclusion, causal histories, and train-only fitting.
use_when: engineering temporal features
using historical aggregates
avoid_when: never relax for a candidate

title: Canonical validation prediction artifact
summary: Defines the exact NPZ arrays, canonical validation order, length, dtype, and finiteness requirements enforced after training.
use_when: changing data loading
changing inference
debugging contract failures
avoid_when: sorting or filtering validation without restoring canonical order

title: Starter Kit empirical priors for experiment selection
summary: Uses committee-reported negative results to deprioritize broad static-feature bundles and capacity-only scaling while prioritizing ranking objectives, causal histories, auxiliary tasks, watch-time modeling, and temporal robustness.
use_when: generating hypotheses
ranking candidate experiments
checking whether a proposal repeats a known low-yield direction
avoid_when: treating committee guidance as a hard ban or as measured evidence for the current parent

title: Adversarial perturbation regularization for embedding rankers
summary: Add a small worst-case norm-bounded perturbation to learned user, video, and optional metadata embeddings during training, then optimize the ordinary ranking loss plus the perturbed-loss term. Start from a converged non-adversarial checkpoint and perturb only dense embedding representations, not raw IDs or causal aggregate inputs.
use_when: Embedding-based rankers overfit despite ordinary dropout and weight decay.
Validation performance is unstable across seeds or degrades sharply for sparse entities.
A robust regularization experiment is justified after a strong baseline exists.
avoid_when: The baseline is underfit or training is already compute-constrained.
Perturbation strength has not been bounded relative to typical embedding norms.
Using a highly brittle listwise implementation that cannot safely perform a second forward/backward pass.

title: Causal sequence-view contrastive pretraining before ranking fine-tuning
summary: For a causal sequence encoder, pretrain user-history representations with two independently augmented views of the same strictly prior interaction sequence, then fine-tune on the supervised long-view ranking task. Use conservative history cropping, masking, and short subsequence views; never include interactions at or after the scored impression.
use_when: Using the causal sequence-transformer ranker with enough historical events.
Sparse or short histories make supervised sequence training unstable.
The supervised sequence model underperforms simpler ID-plus-MLP models despite adequate optimization.
avoid_when: The selected production candidate is a non-sequential MLP ranker.
History augmentation changes the meaning of the sequence, such as aggressively deleting rare but decisive recent events.
There is insufficient compute for a clearly separated pretraining and fine-tuning comparison.

title: Group-complete, label-stratified minibatching
summary: Build minibatches from complete displayed candidate groups rather than independent impressions. Stratify group sampling by zero-positive, mixed-label, and all-positive groups, while ensuring every mixed group retains all of its displayed candidates so pairwise and listwise losses see valid within-user comparisons.
use_when: Training RankNet, LambdaRank-style, or ListNet objectives.
The primary metrics are computed within user candidate groups.
Mixed-label groups are uncommon enough that ordinary row sampling yields many uninformative batches.
avoid_when: Training a strictly pointwise-only baseline where group reconstruction materially limits throughput.
Candidate-group identifiers cannot be reconstructed reliably.
required_features: candidate order or stable impression identifier

title: Validation-safe metric-aligned checkpoint averaging
summary: Save checkpoints at predetermined epochs, select a small contiguous late-training window using the primary validation composite, and average compatible model weights before emitting the canonical prediction artifact. Use the exact same checkpoint schedule and one predeclared tie rule across experiments to reduce variance without repeatedly searching validation noise.
use_when: Training curves are noisy across late epochs.
The model uses a stable optimizer trajectory and identical parameter shapes across checkpoints.
Experiment IDs are scarce and an inexpensive robustness improvement is preferable to broad hyperparameter sweeps.
avoid_when: Training has clear late-epoch divergence or abrupt learning-rate restarts.
Batch-normalization statistics or incompatible optimizer/model states make direct averaging unsafe.
The checkpoint window would be chosen after inspecting many unrelated validation variants.

title: Warm-started hard-pair curriculum within displayed groups
summary: Warm-start with uniformly sampled positive-negative pairs inside each mixed candidate group, then progressively emphasize pairs whose current score margins are small or incorrectly ordered. Retain a fixed random-pair fraction and cap per-group pair counts to prevent a few large or noisy groups from dominating updates.
use_when: A pairwise or LambdaRank-style objective is already competitive.
Training has many valid positive-negative pairs per mixed group.
Early pairwise training is stable but later epochs show little nDCG@5 improvement.
avoid_when: The model is still near-random; mine hard pairs only after a pointwise warm start.
Groups have only one or two valid pairs, making mining effectively meaningless.
Observed hard pairs are suspected to be dominated by label noise.
